paper.title_en: Periodic orbits and numerical-kludge gravitational-wave signatures of an <math altimg="si121.svg" display="inline" id="d1e648"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> Einstein–Skyrme black hole
paper.abstract_en: We investigate timelike geodesic dynamics, periodic zoom–whirl orbits, and associated numerical-kludge gravitational-wave proxies in the black-hole solution of <math altimg="si121.svg" display="inline" id="d1e877"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> Einstein–Skyrme theory. We examine how black hole phenomenological deformation parameters affect the horizon structure, effective potential, circular orbits, and bound periodic trajectories. Particular attention is paid to the marginally bound orbit and innermost stable circular orbit. Periodic orbits are characterized using the established rational taxonomy <math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e892"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mi>w</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> and their closure is verified numerically through the accumulated azimuthal advance. Representative trajectories are then used to construct leading-order numerical-kludge waveform proxies using a quadrupole prescription. The resulting numerical-kludge waveforms exhibit qualitative variations in amplitude modulation, phase evolution, and temporal morphology associated with the orbital topology and phenomenological Skyrme parameters. Since the Einstein–Skyrme spacetime possesses an asymptotic solid-angle deficit, these waveforms are interpreted as qualitative quadrupole proxies rather than quantitative gravitational-wave predictions. The comparison with Schwarzschild spacetime illustrates the sensitivity of periodic orbital motion and approximate waveform morphology to the modified background geometry, without establishing observational distinguishability.
